Decide only from the text below; do not use tools.
Root question: Can molecular mapping of AAV capsid-receptor interactions on brain microvascular endothelial cells determine which AAV variants transcytose across the blood-brain barrier versus remain intracellular, and for which capsid-receptor binding signatures?
Option record: {\"id\":\"Structural coverage of capsid–receptor–glycan complexes\",\"title\":\"Structural coverage of capsid–receptor–glycan complexes\",\"summary\":\"Exhaustive AlphaFold-Multimer, cryo-ET and MD modelling of capsid–receptor–glycan complexes across many variants, receptors and pH values would turn epitope geometry and pH-resolved kinetics from a per-complex experiment into a computed prior (method precedent: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11381518).\",\"root_link\":\"Bears on the \\"for which capsid–receptor binding signatures\\" half of the question — whether the epitope-geometry and pH-resolved-kinetics components of a signature can be computed instead of measured per complex.\",\"compute_open\":\"Model runs (capsid–receptor–glycan complexes predicted per pH condition): the largest amount a cited source reports is AlphaFold-Multimer runs of 5 structural models per capsid peptide with up to 20 recycles, paired with cryo-ET sub-tomogram averaging of 85,135 symmetry-expanded particles (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11381518), and what is still unknown above that amount is whether any scale of computed coverage recovers epitope geometry and pH-resolved off-rates accurately enough to classify transcytosis versus retention, since the only quantitative pH-resolved benchmark in hand is a single measured pair (ALPL–VCAP-102, K_D ≈ 20 nM at pH 7.4 with rapid dissociation at pH 5.5: https://www.cell.com/molecular-therapy/fulltext/S1525-0016(25)00373-9).\",\"sequential\":\"One run is a chain of roughly 10^9–10^12 integration steps at about 2 fs each, every step waiting on the previous coordinates, and a full answer needs several independent replicas per (capsid, receptor, pH) condition, with one replica keeping a GPU-resident MD engine busy for its whole length (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9281402/). The steps must run in order inside a single trajectory, but the answer can be assembled instead from many short independent trajectories started at the same time, which pays off when metastable states separate timescales so replicas decorrelate and weak scaling of independent runs beats strong scaling of one run (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9476681/); the nearest source that tried it is adaptive-sampling Markov state modelling, where wall-clock efficiency scaled linearly up to 5,000 parallel simulations per iteration (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3637129/).\",\"source_urls\":[\"https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11381518\",\"https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9281402/\",\"https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3637129/\"]}
Card:
card:question: Can computed capsid–receptor structures and pH-resolved MD contact lifetimes classify which AAV capsids cross brain endothelium versus stay inside cells?
card:hypothesis: Epitope geometry from AlphaFold plus pH contact survival from many short replicas separates transcytosing LRP6/ALPL binders from retained capsids [s_lrp6][s_moyer].
card:sequential_part: One trajectory's 10^9–10^12 ordered 2-fs steps, each frame waiting on the last [s_jones].
card:method: Many short independent replicas run at once; contacts decorrelate inside each replica, so weak scaling beats one long run [s_kasson][s_kutzner_ens].
card:if_lever: At 32 ten-ns replicas per condition the score reaches AUC ≥ 0.9 and pH ratio > 2, matching the 320-ns run [s_moyer].
card:if_not: At 8–32 replicas the score stays at AUC ≤ 0.75 with no pH difference; the 320-ns run agrees, so more replicas do not help.
card:test_summary: ColabFold AlphaFold-Multimer on 24 peptide–receptor complexes, then 32 ten-ns GROMACS replicas per pair at pH 7.4 and 5.5 on 8 V100s; compared with 320-ns sequential runs and published binding, domain and pH-release results [s_lrp6][s_moyer].
card:closest_prior: Adaptive-sampling Markov models matched one long villin run with up to 5,000 parallel simulations per iteration [s_bowman]; capsid work used 5 AlphaFold models per peptide [s_lrp6].
card:left_open: Whether computed pH-resolved contact lifetimes classify transcytosis versus retention at all; only one pair has measured pH kinetics [s_moyer].
card:anchor: Reproduce the published AlphaFold-Multimer result: capsid peptides X1 and CAP-Mac bind LRP6 domain 1, not domains 3 and 4 [s_lrp6].
card:limits: Ten-ns contact-survival proxies, not millisecond off-rates. Peptide–domain fragments in water, not full glycosylated capsids. Six pairs, no cell-level transcytosis measured.
